## Additional Features - **Building Collision** — A buildings index is included for all non-filtered buildings, each carrying a per-building foundation depth in in-game meters. Depths scale with building height and footprint width and are bounded to the **−10 m** to **−80 m** range: single-family homes and low-rise structures anchor at the floor, while the tallest towers with deep piles reach the cap. Freestanding towers, masts, chimneys, and other slender non-occupiable structures are detected by shape and floored to the **−10 m** minimum. Foundation depths drive underground tunnel-clearance collision and are also emitted as a visual `foundations` pmtiles layer visible on the in-game map. Building geometry and heights both come from the ZBGIS Budova national building registry, whose per-building heights are measured from airborne LiDAR (DMR 5.0) and cover the large majority of Slovak buildings. The remainder, which the registry records without a measured height, are treated as single-storey at a height calibrated for their building function. - **Water Depth Index** — A water depth index restricts track placement in water bodies. Slovakia is landlocked, so all water (the Danube and other rivers, lakes, reservoirs) uses a flat **−5 m** index that prevents surface-level track placement. - **Place Name Labels** — Three layers of place name labels are embedded in the map: - _City labels_ — The bundle's anchor cities and regional capitals (krajské mestá) at the metropolitan scale. - _Municipality labels_ — Names of all municipalities (_obce_, including the Bratislava and Košice city boroughs _mestské časti_) within the map boundary. - _Neighborhood labels_ — Sub-municipal settlement names from the SODB statistical hierarchy (_časti obcí_ and basic settlement units _základné sídelné jednotky_). ## Methodology This map is generated through a six-phase pipeline that transforms Slovak government census, building, and employment statistics into georeferenced origin/destination demand points. **Point Seeding:** Candidate points are placed within each basic settlement unit (_základná sídelná jednotka_ / ZSJ) using population-weighted centroids derived from the SODB 2021 per-ZSJ population counts and the native 1 km census grid, dasymetrically distributed against the ZBGIS Budova national building registry filtered by its building-function (BFC) use-class taxonomy. **Mesh Reconciliation:** Initial point populations are refined by solving a constrained convex optimization that approximates each point's mass to residential and economic mesh ideals while preserving per-municipality (_obec_) SODB 2021 census totals. Sub-municipal chochos cascade through the SODB statistical hierarchy — municipality parts (_časti obcí_) and basic settlement units (ZSJ) within them. **Aggregation:** Workplace mass is anchored to the SODB 2021 place-of-work census counts per municipality, so employees are placed where they actually work rather than at a registered head-office address. The sector composition is disaggregated by NACE Rev 2 economic-activity section using the register-based workplace-method employment series from the ŠÚ SR DATAcube, with Eurostat national-accounts splits for the sub-sections the register series does not separate. Each building's implied worker density follows the sector composition of its BFC use-class, calibrated to the municipal employment total. **Commute Assignment:** Commute flows are assigned from the SODB 2021 pair-wise municipality-to-municipality journey-to-work matrix (_dochádzka do zamestnania_), so origin/destination pairs follow the actually-observed census commuting behaviour rather than a synthetic gravity fit. **Special Demand Injection:** Non-commuter demand generators — airports, universities, hospitals, cultural venues, and tourism attractions — are injected as an additive layer as per-facility coverage lands; see the Special Demand section above for the current roster included in this bundle. **Layout Reconciliation:** A final spatial pass resolves point overlaps and ensures map clickability while keeping special-demand locations fixed. ## Data Sources All demand modeling is derived from freely available Slovak government statistical datasets and public geospatial resources. ### Census & Demographics - **2021 Census** (SODB 2021 — _Sčítanie obyvateľov, domov a bytov 2021_: per-obec and per-ZSJ population and employment, the place-of-work anchor, and the pair-wise obec × obec journey-to-work matrix, accessed via the gis.scitanie.sk ArcGIS services) — [ŠÚ SR / scitanie.sk](https://www.scitanie.sk/) - **Workplace Employment** (ŠÚ SR DATAcube `pr3113rr` — register-based employees by workplace method per okres × NACE Rev 2 section;
